**Final finding: compliant — no redline, no comment.**

This is my last call on this rule; the position is settled and I'm not making further changes.

**Why compliant.** IBM holds no audit, inspection, verification or record/system-access right over Bluefly anywhere in the agreement. Searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "monitor" and "premises" return nothing; "records" appears only in the § 9.1 liability carve-out. Every section that could plausibly host a usage-verification right — §§ 4.1, 4.2, 11.5, 12.1, 13.2 and 14.1–14.20 — contains none.

**§ 11.3 is not an audit hook.** It is a breach-investigation and remedy provision tied to the § 11.2(b) content/acceptable-use warranties: IBM may investigate, then restrict Service access, require Content removal, terminate for cause or pursue other remedies, with a best-efforts notice undertaking. It confers no access to our premises, systems, personnel, books or records and imposes no audit cost or cooperation burden.

**On the failing deterministic check.** "Audit frequency limited" fails only because there is no audit clause to carry a frequency cap — an artifact of absence, which the verifier's own reasoning confirms. No walk-away trigger is present, since neither an audit right nor system access is granted. Repairing this check by inserting frequency, notice or cost limits would manufacture a verification right in IBM's favour that the contract does not currently give it, contrary to the rule's protective purpose and the instruction not to flag terms favourable to us. That is the one change I have declined to make across all three passes.

**Carried forward for the negotiation file:** § 11.3's investigation right is uncapped in frequency and its notice commitment is best-efforts with emergency and legal-requirement carve-outs — acceptable as drafted, but this rule should be re-run if § 11.3 is ever expanded to reach our records or systems.
